title: Squid Game cost Netflix $21.4M. What was it really worth? 🦑
description:

Sources: Bloomberg, Al Jazeera (Oct 2021). The characters are not advisers.
Illustrative only. Not financial advice.
cta: The show or the subscribers: which was Netflix buying? Comment

lines.text: Squid Game cost Netflix $21.4M. What was it worth?
In under a month, 132M people pressed play on it.
Netflix sold no tickets for it. So how does a show pay Netflix back?
Inside Netflix, every show gets a score in dollars: its impact value.
Double what it cost? Far more than that.
Netflix's own papers valued Squid Game at $891.1M. That's about 41.6× what it cost.
The show, or the members it pulled in: which was Netflix paying for? So

All 4 facts confirmed on the Al Jazeera/Bloomberg page (WebFetch): 'generated $891.1 million in impact value, a metric the company uses to assess the performance from individual shows'; 'cost just $21.4 million to produce - about $2.4 million an episode'; 'About 132 million people have watched at least two minutes ... in the show's first 23 days'. Verify list met: $891.1M is said as 'valued', never made/earned; 'Netflix's own papers' fits a confidential Netflix document Netflix's attorney objected to disclosing without disputing; figures are season one and the script never extends them to later seasons, with 'Data: Bloomberg · Oct 2021' on screen. No advice, no adviser persona, tone fine, description ends with the disclaimer. Notes: 'every show gets a score' slightly generalises 'a metric used for individual shows'; saying 'season one' or 'in 2021' once would head off viewers thinking of seasons 2-3; 'pressed play' understates the 2-minute bar (safe).
